deviations.what: Add a logprob verifier between Tier 1 and the proposal: after Needle3 selects an operation, a local LFM2.5 model is asked a fixed yes/no question ('For <request> the solution is <operation>. Correct?') and nvsh reads the next-token log-probabilities of yes vs no (one prefill, one token, nothing generated) as the confidence signal; a multiple-choice variant reads the next-token distribution over lettered operations plus 'none'. This replaces Needle's learned confidence head as the propose/ask/escalate signal, works for a fine-tuned Needle that reports no confidence, and is calibrated (temperature/Platt) on the corpus dev split. It is NOT the safety mechanism: approval, the single-call rule, table validation and grounding are unchanged. nvsh/tiers/toolchat.py gains a score() call returning next-token logprobs; the benchmark adds calibration metrics and compares Needle's own confidence vs yes/no vs multiple-choice, on base and post-trained LFM2.5; vLLM is tried before llama.cpp because prefill speed is what matters here.
deviations.reason: Measured: Needle3's confidence is a learned probe head, scored a wrong pick 1.0, is None for a fine-tuned model, and the shipped engine exposes no logits; LFM2.5 runtimes expose real token logprobs over the OpenAI-compatible API. Operator proposed the yes/no logit structure and approved this departure on 2026-09-19.

deviations.what: Fine-tuning and sharing, for all tier models: (1) tuned weights and the training data are published under the public Hugging Face org jetson-ai-lab, hard-coded in nvsh's pins with a config override (repo + revision + sha256 together); names follow <base>-nvsh-<task>: models jetson-ai-lab/needle3-nvsh-ops and jetson-ai-lab/lfm2.5-350m-nvsh-triage (+ a -GGUF repo for the llama.cpp build), dataset jetson-ai-lab/nvsh-ops; version tags ops<N>-r<M>, nvsh pins by commit + sha256, and a tuned pin records the operation-table hash it was trained on (mismatch => doctor reports it and the tier falls back to stock). (2) LFM2.5 fine-tuning moves from non-goal (c18) to documented recipe: instructions for unsloth, unsloth-cli and a remote Hugging Face run; Needle keeps cactus-needle's own JAX LoRA path (unsloth cannot train it). nvsh ships recipes, the dataset exporter and the pins; it still runs no training itself and uploads nothing on its own -- publishing stays an operator action (c17 unchanged).
deviations.reason: Operator request 2026-09-19: created the jetson-ai-lab HF org, asked for unsloth/unsloth-cli/HF-remote fine-tune instructions, and to share data and weights with one naming format for all models. Unsloth targets HF-transformers models, so this necessarily brings LFM2.5 tuning into scope.

deltas.behavior_text: The pinned engine is extracted from the verified wheel and the verified stock weights are staged into an nvsh-owned HOME for the child only, so stock Needle3 keeps a real confidence, starts no nested subprocess and never downloads; the plan had the worker pass the weights path directly, which cactus-needle treats as a tuned model (confidence None).

The d1 yes/no check runs last (after table, grounding and rendering) and is asked about the grounded arguments; a failed baseline measurement is retried instead of cached. Its three thresholds are unmeasured placeholders.

A tier request holds a lease from the moment it opens, so the idle sweep cannot close the tiers under an in-flight selection; a client that disconnects cancels its tier session (cooperatively: an in-flight select, bounded at 10 s, is not interrupted).

The benchmark grounds against a fixture machine declared in the corpus (--live for the host), reports one row per request and accuracy per request kind; a target that was not measured prints 'not measured', never pass.

Measured through the shipped path, stock Needle3 reaches about half of the c20 accuracy and decline targets on the Spark; routing therefore ships opt-in only and the accuracy work (corpus as a grid, LoRA, verifier thresholds) is recorded in docs/tiers-improving-accuracy.md. Thor and AGX Orin are not measured yet.
needle can never be persisted as the default agent: nvsh agent use, nvsh setup (flag, @name, model-qualified, alias) and nvsh doctor all read one registry table.

Publishing under the jetson-ai-lab Hugging Face org with the <base>-nvsh-<task> naming and ops<N>-r<M> tags is documented in docs/needle-finetune.md; loading a tuned model (tuned pin, operation-table hash check, config override) is NOT built.
needle can never be persisted as the default agent: nvsh agent use, nvsh setup (flag, @name, model-qualified, alias) and nvsh doctor all read one registry table.

Documentation only, not program behaviour: docs/needle-finetune.md records the d2 publishing convention (jetson-ai-lab organisation, <base>-nvsh-<task> names, ops<N>-r<M> tags). nvsh does not implement any of it yet: no tuned pin, no operation-table hash check, no config override, no upload.

The pinned engine is extracted from the verified wheel and the verified stock weights are staged into an nvsh-owned HOME for the child only, so stock Needle3 keeps a real confidence, starts no nested subprocess and never downloads.

The d1 yes/no check runs last (after table, grounding and rendering) and is asked about the grounded arguments; a failed baseline measurement is retried instead of cached. Its thresholds are unmeasured placeholders and it has never run against a model inside the router.

A tier request holds a lease from the moment it opens, so the idle sweep cannot close the tiers under an in-flight selection; a client that disconnects cancels its tier session (cooperatively: an in-flight select, bounded at 10 s, is not interrupted).

The benchmark grounds against a fixture machine declared in the corpus (--live for the host), reports one row per request and accuracy per request kind; a target that was not measured prints 'not measured', never pass.
